reasons.text: Indeed, Will Osula was forced off at half time after twisting his ankle and is now a major doubt for Monday night, so Yoane Wissa should be restored to the number nine role.

Goals from William Osula (£5.8m) and Harvey Barnes (£6.1m) secured the points, although the biggest FPL talking point came before kick-off, with Yoane Wissa (£6.1m) and Malick Thiaw (£5.0m) both benched.
Matthias Jaissle made five changes to his starting XI, with Wissa, Thiaw and Sven Botman (£5.0m) among those dropping to the bench.

While it may be tough to ditch Wissa before he faces Crystal Palace on Sunday, there are no guarantees that he will continue in a number nine role at Selhurst Park, particularly with Will Osula (£5.8m) building his fitness.

You get the feeling that things could quickly unravel for Newcastle if they fall behind, too, so there are surely safer bets than Wissa for the upcoming period, like Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6.0m) and Nicolas Jackson (£6.6m).
VERDICT: BUY THIERNO BARRY Another in-form player, Thierno Barry (£5.7m) is fourth among forwards for points (55), with six goals and one assist in 10 matches.
Barry has failed to convert 16 of his 22 big chances in 2026/27 so far.

Barry has notched 13 goal involvements (10 goals, three assists) in all competitions so far this season, most recently a quick-fire brace in the Blues' 3-1 come-from-behind victory over Coventry City prior to the international break.

After three goals, an assist and 25 points over the latest two Fantasy Premier League (FPL) Gameweeks, Everton’s Thierno Barry (£5.7m) is currently the second most-bought player of this international break.

Barry’s goals took him to double figures across all competitions for the campaign, with only Erling Haaland (nine) and Alexander Isak (seven) having struck more Premier League goals this season than Barry (six).
Asked about his strong form, Barry told evertontv : “I'm very happy because it's always a pleasure to score and I'm so happy to do my first assist in the Premier League.
BARRY FRONT AND CENTRE Above: Everton players sorted by shots and big chances (BC) in Gameweek 10 It was the usual mix of the sublime and the ridiculous from Barry.

The Toffees fell behind shortly after the half-time interval at Hill Dickinson Stadium, before a brace from Thierno Barry and a well-taken strike by Dewsbury-Hall sealed a third consecutive win in the space of eight days.
But Barry proved too hot for Coventry to handle, netting twice in the space of just five minutes to turn the game in Everton 's favour.

reasons.text: Palmer was left out of the England squad for the World Cup in the summer after an injury-plagued season for Chelsea and then pulled out of the squad in September on the basis of ‘load management’.
Palmer was omitted from Tuchel's latest squad despite featuring regularly for Chelsea under Xabi Alonso this season, having previously withdrawn from international duty because of injury concerns.

Palmer , left ‌out of England 's World Cup squad this year after a persistent groin ‌injury affected his form, was called up by coach ‌Thomas Tuchel for Nations League fixtures against Spain, the Czech ‌Republic and Croatia in September and October.
Asked about Palmer's exclusion ‌after England's 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley, goalscorer Rogers told ​the BBC: "He wants to be here.

It’s been suggested that Palmer – who’s got five goals and three assists for the Blues this season – is being punished by Tuchel, who said the forward “misses too many opportunities” to impress for England when he pulled out of the previous squad due to ‘load management’.
Beyond that, Morgan Rogers, Morgan Gibbs-White, Eberechi Eze, Cole Palmer and Phil Foden have all competed for that position over the past 18 months.

Each of them offers something a little different to Bellingham: Eze and Palmer, for example, have the deftness of pass, while Foden and Rogers are capable of arriving at the edge of the box for a finesse finish into the bottom corner.
England manager Thomas Tuchel said in September that Palmer had missed "too many opportunities" to play for the national team after he pulled out of the squad with an injury.
Palmer, 24, who was omitted from Tuchel's World Cup squad, has had an inconsistent start to the season at Stamford Bridge.
Cole Palmer: Tuchel aims seven-word 'attitude' dig at Chelsea star as England mask slips Cole Palmer has been left out of the England squad by Thomas Tuchel.
Tuchel called Palmer up for his first post-World Cup roster only to be disappointed by his swift withdrawal through injury .

Palmer was the headline omission from the group named this morning for the Nations League games with Croatia and Spain and has seemingly paid the price for withdrawing from the last camp with a minor injury.

reasons.text: Indeed, Will Osula was forced off at half time after twisting his ankle and is now a major doubt for Monday night, so Yoane Wissa should be restored to the number nine role.

Goals from William Osula (£5.8m) and Harvey Barnes (£6.1m) secured the points, although the biggest FPL talking point came before kick-off, with Yoane Wissa (£6.1m) and Malick Thiaw (£5.0m) both benched.
Matthias Jaissle made five changes to his starting XI, with Wissa, Thiaw and Sven Botman (£5.0m) among those dropping to the bench.

While it may be tough to ditch Wissa before he faces Crystal Palace on Sunday, there are no guarantees that he will continue in a number nine role at Selhurst Park, particularly with Will Osula (£5.8m) building his fitness.

You get the feeling that things could quickly unravel for Newcastle if they fall behind, too, so there are surely safer bets than Wissa for the upcoming period, like Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6.0m) and Nicolas Jackson (£6.6m).
VERDICT: BUY THIERNO BARRY Another in-form player, Thierno Barry (£5.7m) is fourth among forwards for points (55), with six goals and one assist in 10 matches.
Barry has failed to convert 16 of his 22 big chances in 2026/27 so far.

Barry has notched 13 goal involvements (10 goals, three assists) in all competitions so far this season, most recently a quick-fire brace in the Blues' 3-1 come-from-behind victory over Coventry City prior to the international break.

After three goals, an assist and 25 points over the latest two Fantasy Premier League (FPL) Gameweeks, Everton’s Thierno Barry (£5.7m) is currently the second most-bought player of this international break.

Barry’s goals took him to double figures across all competitions for the campaign, with only Erling Haaland (nine) and Alexander Isak (seven) having struck more Premier League goals this season than Barry (six).
Asked about his strong form, Barry told evertontv : “I'm very happy because it's always a pleasure to score and I'm so happy to do my first assist in the Premier League.
BARRY FRONT AND CENTRE Above: Everton players sorted by shots and big chances (BC) in Gameweek 10 It was the usual mix of the sublime and the ridiculous from Barry.

The Toffees fell behind shortly after the half-time interval at Hill Dickinson Stadium, before a brace from Thierno Barry and a well-taken strike by Dewsbury-Hall sealed a third consecutive win in the space of eight days.
But Barry proved too hot for Coventry to handle, netting twice in the space of just five minutes to turn the game in Everton 's favour.

reasons.text: The French striker also produced the assist for Dewsbury-Hall's goal against Frank Lampard's side – and it comes as no surprise to the Toffees' No.8 to see his teammate thriving.

The Toffees fell behind shortly after the half-time interval at Hill Dickinson Stadium, before a brace from Thierno Barry and a well-taken strike by Dewsbury-Hall sealed a third consecutive win in the space of eight days.

The Blues moved into fifth in the Premier League table ahead of this weekend's round of matches, having to come from behind to Yann Gboho's 52nd-minute opener courtesy of a quickfire double from Thierno Barry, before the Frenchman turned provider to see Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall seal the win nine minutes from time.

The Blues came from behind to beat Frank Lampard’s Sky Blues at Hill Dickinson Stadium – with Barry netting Everton’s first and second of the game, before Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall added a third courtesy of the Frenchman's assist.

Three points – which lifted Everton into fifth place in the Premier League table ahead of this weekend's round of matches – were then secured against Frank Lampard's top-flight newcomers nine minutes from time when Barry slid in Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall to blast past Carl Rushworth.
A slick one-two between George and Dewsbury-Hall on nine minutes – that started with a lovely backheel from the winger – allowed George to play Barry through on the right side of the penalty area.

Garner joins Harrison Armstrong and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall in central midfield, flanked by wingers Tyrique George and Dibling, with striker Thierno Barry looking to add to his tally of 10 goal involvements for the season so far.
DEWSBURY-HALL EXCELLENT + UNLUCKY TO BLANK Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall (£6.6m) was named Man of the Match, and few would argue with that.

reasons.text: Having provided an assist in the Red Devils’ victory over Turkey last Thursday, De Cuyper followed that up with a goal in Belgium’s riotous 4-1 win against Italy on Sunday.
It was De Cuyper’s goal that proved the catalyst for his side’s comeback.

He had two goal involvements in 18 minutes and a hand in a third in the opening 4-0 win against Aston Villa Matty Cash spent the whole first half caught between two jobs: following De Cuyper inside or holding his line.
It’s been a whirlwind ‘out of position’ ride with De Cuyper this season, and there’s little sign of a slowdown.
De Cuyper’s not an issue for now, then, even if Luka Vuskovic (£5.2m) will likely end up being the long, long-term best pick at the back.

Brighton and Hove Albion duo Maxim De Cuyper (£5.3m) and Pascal Gross (£6.2m) are at the summit of FPL’s points table: But up next for the pair: two potentially tricky away days at Liverpool and Manchester City.
De Cuyper had to content himself with ‘just’ six points against the Gunners, and his sole blank so far came against the Blues.
De Cuyper is a defender in FPL but is regularly used in advanced areas.

reasons.text: Having provided an assist in the Red Devils’ victory over Turkey last Thursday, De Cuyper followed that up with a goal in Belgium’s riotous 4-1 win against Italy on Sunday.
It was De Cuyper’s goal that proved the catalyst for his side’s comeback.

He had two goal involvements in 18 minutes and a hand in a third in the opening 4-0 win against Aston Villa Matty Cash spent the whole first half caught between two jobs: following De Cuyper inside or holding his line.
It’s been a whirlwind ‘out of position’ ride with De Cuyper this season, and there’s little sign of a slowdown.
De Cuyper’s not an issue for now, then, even if Luka Vuskovic (£5.2m) will likely end up being the long, long-term best pick at the back.

With well-owned defenders Riccardo Calafiori (£6.0m) and Maxim De Cuyper (£5.3m) set to face tricky away fixtures at Liverpool and Manchester City in Gameweek 9, plenty of Fantasy managers will be in the market for a new defender ahead of Saturday’s deadline.

Brighton and Hove Albion duo Maxim De Cuyper (£5.3m) and Pascal Gross (£6.2m) are at the summit of FPL’s points table: But up next for the pair: two potentially tricky away days at Liverpool and Manchester City.

evidence.text: Indeed, Will Osula was forced off at half time after twisting his ankle and is now a major doubt for Monday night, so Yoane Wissa should be restored to the number nine role.

Goals from William Osula (£5.8m) and Harvey Barnes (£6.1m) secured the points, although the biggest FPL talking point came before kick-off, with Yoane Wissa (£6.1m) and Malick Thiaw (£5.0m) both benched.
Matthias Jaissle made five changes to his starting XI, with Wissa, Thiaw and Sven Botman (£5.0m) among those dropping to the bench.

While it may be tough to ditch Wissa before he faces Crystal Palace on Sunday, there are no guarantees that he will continue in a number nine role at Selhurst Park, particularly with Will Osula (£5.8m) building his fitness.

You get the feeling that things could quickly unravel for Newcastle if they fall behind, too, so there are surely safer bets than Wissa for the upcoming period, like Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6.0m) and Nicolas Jackson (£6.6m).
